features.title: One library, many places
features.body: Films, Series, Search and Home combine your computers, NAS folders and cloud. A small line says where each copy lives.

features.title: One profile that follows you
features.body: Link your profile across your servers. What you watched and where you stopped follows you from one server to the next.

features.title: Google Drive as a source
features.body: Stream from the Drive folders you choose, in short pieces. Until Google approves Theia's own connection, connecting may ask for your own Google client.

features.title: NAS folders
features.body: A NAS share mounted on a server joins the library, and your history survives if it sleeps. The UGREEN test kit is unverified on a real UGREEN so far.

features.title: Servers and sources, in settings
features.body: Add, rename and reconnect servers and sources on one settings page, each with a small icon: tower, laptop, NAS or cloud. Pair a machine with a short code.

features.title: One page for every title
features.body: The same title page whichever source holds the file: play, resume, mark as watched, leave an opinion and preview a scene.

features.title: Watched means watched
features.body: Anti-spoil shows an episode's artwork once you pass its last fifth, and a file's own ending-credits chapter counts as watched.

features.title: An update that keeps everything
features.body: Upgrading from 4.4.6 keeps your library, profiles and history. Checked on a real 4.4.6 installation, rollback included.

features.title: Your library on your phone
features.body: An Android app plays your library from your server, with your profile and the places where you stopped. Download the APK from the release page.

features.title: Android TV and Google TV (beta)
features.body: The same app opens a television presentation you drive with the remote, and keeps AC-3, E-AC-3 and DTS sound when your television can take it. A beta: tell us what you find.

v5.laterIntro: Planned, but not promised for this release. Each one is announced once it is proven on real hardware.

later.title: A phone without a server, and casting
later.body: A phone that reads your NAS or Drive on its own, and casting to a screen. Announced once built and checked.

later.title: ARM computers

v5.title: Generation 5
v5.lead: One unified library across servers, NAS shares and Google Drive, a profile that follows you, and the Android app.

v4.title: Generation 4
v4.lead: Household profiles, friends, opinions, private watch-party rooms, direct WireGuard remote access and signed interface packs.

v3.title: Generation 3 — from 3.3
v3.lead: The split into server, native desktop player and terminal setup, then the six desktop targets.

v5.0.0.title: Everything you own, in one library
v5.0.0.summary: Opens Generation 5 by combining multiple Theia servers, NAS shares and Google Drive folders into a single library, alongside linked profiles and the Android application.
changes: Combines multiple Theia servers, mounted NAS folders (history survives NAS sleep; the UGREEN test kit remains unverified on a physical UGREEN) and chosen Google Drive folders streamed in short pieces (until Google approves Theia's own OAuth client, connecting may request your own Google client).
Links your profile across your servers so watched state and resume positions follow you from one machine to the next with deterministic conflict and rewatch rules.
Adds a unified Servers and sources page in player settings and web administration, with tower, laptop, NAS and cloud icons plus short-code machine pairing.

Shows the sender's name and profile photo on incoming friend requests immediately before acceptance, even when their server is offline; redesigns the connect and cold-start screen to remember up to six servers, surface explicit mDNS discovery states and rest on a generated brass glyph canvas.

Unifies the title page across all sources; reveals anti-spoil episode artwork past the last fifth and counts ending-credits chapters as watched; hides the pointer with idle controls during playback; holds Space (play) for 220 ms to run at 2x speed outside watch-party rooms.

Ships the Android phone app (Android 8.0+, handheld controls, picture-in-picture, lock-screen media session and cross-device resume, checked on Xiaomi POCO with Android 16) and an Android TV / Google TV beta with remote navigation and AC-3, E-AC-3 and DTS passthrough where supported.
Upgrading from 4.4.6 preserves your library, profiles and history (checked on a 4.4.6 installation, rollback included); Windows and Linux ARM64 desktop setups remain at 4.2.1.

v4.4.6.title: Remote access recovers, and the player steps out of the way
v4.4.6.summary: Shell update making automatic remote access resilient to busy UDP ports and router restarts, fixing the browser administration link and keeping restored windows clean.
changes: Reserves a free UDP port automatically when the preferred remote-access port is busy, and shows a clear error when a manually chosen port is already taken.
Checks UPnP and NAT-PMP port forwarding periodically and recreates dropped router rules automatically after a router restart (verified on a Freebox v9).
Restores opening server administration in the system browser with a Retry button on failure, and stops Alt-Tab focus return on a maximized window from holding controls over a playing film.
Publishes desktop setups for Windows x64, Ubuntu 24.04 x64, macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel; Windows and Linux ARM64 desktop setups stay at 4.2.1.

v4.4.5.title: Filled profile circles, interactive photo framing and fresh-install chapters
v4.4.5.summary: Signed interface pack improving small profile avatars, adding interactive crop and zoom in the profile editor, and waiting for FFmpeg chapter inspection on fresh installs.
changes: Scales profile photos of 512 px or smaller to fill the circular frame instead of leaving dark margins around small images.
Adds pointer drag, keyboard nudging and zoom controls when framing a profile photo in Customize profile; cropping runs locally and metadata is stripped on the server.
Downloads SHA-256-verified FFmpeg (~80 MB) in the background on a fresh install's first episode and checks up to two minutes for chapter markers so Skip opening and Next episode appear.

v4.4.4.title: End-of-episode prompts that step aside
v4.4.4.summary: Signed interface pack refining episode-ending buttons and chapter pills so scrubbing the timeline at the end of an episode is never blocked.
changes: Steps end-of-episode buttons aside and pauses the local next-episode countdown whenever you hover or focus the timeline near the end of an episode (room countdowns continue uninterrupted).
Hides Skip opening and Go to post-credits after eight seconds and brings them back whenever playback controls wake.
Replaces the dark backing card with three distinct pills: a dark Skip opening pill, a light Next episode pill that fills across the 30-second countdown, and a quiet Keep watching pill.

v4.4.3.title: Prerelease ordering in the interface updater
v4.4.3.summary: Signed interface pack fixing semantic-version comparison for tester builds so every 4.4 shell receives final interface updates cleanly.
changes: Fixes prerelease ordering in the UI updater so tester builds such as 4.4.2-test.3 rank older than final releases such as 4.4.2.
Republishes the Ed25519-signed interface pack so level-3 native shells update the interface without re-running the full setup.

v4.4.2.title: Scene previews, chapter flow, richer settings and private rooms
v4.4.2.summary: Major V4 feature update adding exact-frame timeline thumbnails, chapter-driven episode transitions, eight-section settings, spoiler protection, richer presence and invite-only rooms.
changes: Decodes exact-frame timeline hover previews in a second paused engine instance (with server fallback for HDR files) and adds configurable 10 s, 30 s (default) or 60 s skip steps that stack on rapid presses.
Adds manual Skip opening from named chapters, a cancellable 30-second Next episode countdown that stops at a season finale, Go to post-credits scene, and a sleep timer.

Reorganises settings into eight categories (General, Playback, Audio and subtitles, Privacy, Server, Updates, Statistics, Help) with per-series track memory, language priority, forced/SDH preferences, audio device selection, sync offsets, UI scale and customizable shortcuts.
Saves playback progress cleanly during bounded window close and adds a per-series Spoiler protection switch that blurs unwatched episode stills and hides synopses.

Expands friend presence (Online, Inactive, Watching, Offline; Up for a film, Do not disturb, Invisible; navigation-bar avatars and return notices) and makes removing a friend clean up both sides via inbox notice.
Adds private invite-only watch-party rooms with optional join requests from friends.

v4.4.1.title: Opinions between households, and idle presence
v4.4.1.summary: Signed interface pack carrying friend title opinions over Firebase without open router ports and introducing the automatic Inactive state.
changes: Delivers one editable, deletable opinion per title (thumb, date and spoiler blur) between friends through Firebase (theia-friends) without requiring open router ports.
Switches presence to Inactive automatically after five minutes idle, dimming the avatar ring and excluding idle friends from the online count.
Ships as an Ed25519-signed interface pack for 4.4.0 native shells alongside updated standalone servers.

v4.4.0.title: A stable native shell, smaller signed updates
v4.4.0.summary: Splits the frozen native player shell from Ed25519-signed interface packs with automatic rollback, and ships the Firebase friend directory.
changes: Separates the native player shell from Ed25519-signed interface packs that trial-boot on launch and roll back automatically if startup fails.
Includes the Firebase friend directory, offline-capable friend requests (THEIA2- codes alongside legacy THEIA1- codes) and fast presence updates without router port forwarding.
Preserves the playback clock across converted stream reloads, stores offline progress saves in an ordered per-server/per-profile outbox, and disables episode autoplay in rooms.

Publishes desktop setups for Windows x64, Ubuntu 24.04 x64, macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel; Windows and Linux ARM64 desktop setups stay at 4.2.1 due to hosted runner limits while standalone servers ship for all six platforms.

v4.3.1.title: Friend requests that arrive without port forwarding
v4.3.1.summary: Introduces the anonymous Firebase directory for friend codes, offline requests and presence; merged and published directly within 4.4.0 the same day.
changes: Moves friend discovery, friend requests and presence to Firebase Realtime Database (theia-friends) with anonymous sign-in so requests arrive even when a peer's server is off or behind NAT.
Introduces THEIA2-XXXXX-XXXXX friend codes while keeping existing THEIA1- codes working, updates presence within one to two seconds, and shows an explicit unreachable notice when offline.
Keeps media streams, library catalogues and watch history off Firebase; direct WireGuard tunnels remain dedicated to remote playback and rooms.

v4.3.0.title: Title reviews, tabbed title pages, faster startup and macOS setups
v4.3.0.summary: Adds household and friend title reviews, redesigns title pages around tabs and device compatibility checks, trims player weight and restores both macOS setups.
changes: Lets viewers leave a thumb up/down and a 500-character review per title with a spoiler switch, and tints profile rings from each profile's photo.
Redesigns film and series pages with tabs (episodes, synopsis, cast, saga, reviews), a file version chooser and a Playback on this device check.
Shrinks the desktop player binary (11.5 MB vs 15.1 MB) and UI assets (1.7 MB vs 4.5 MB), opens title pages faster and halves CPU usage while searching.
Restores complete macOS Apple Silicon and Intel setups and restarts launchd or systemd services cleanly after in-app updates on macOS and Linux.
Checks online during setup whether a newer installer release exists before writing files.

v4.2.2.title: On-demand quality rungs, and rooms without stray pauses
v4.2.2.summary: Inspects unmeasured films on demand when opening the quality menu and prevents background clicks in a watch party from pausing everyone.
changes: Triggers an immediate FFmpeg stream inspection when opening the quality menu on an unmeasured film so lower quality options appear right away.
Changes clicking the video background inside a watch-party room to wake the controls rather than toggling pause for the whole room.
Highlights the room button while a room is active and removes the misleading down chevron on the solo playback island.
Ships desktop setups for Windows x64 and Ubuntu 24.04 x64 alongside standalone servers for all six platforms.

v4.2.1.title: Shared Windows audio alongside calls, clean fullscreen and verified updates
v4.2.1.summary: Keeps voice calls audible during playback on Windows by default, fixes maximized-to-fullscreen taskbar overlap, and adds SHA-256 setup updates.
changes: Defaults Windows audio to shared mode so Discord and voice calls stay audible beside a film, with an opt-in Untouched sound to the amplifier setting for exclusive bitstream passthrough.
Fixes entering fullscreen from a maximized Windows window so the taskbar never remains on top, and simplifies the solo island back to the end-time clock.
Downloads and SHA-256-verifies the full Windows setup from the in-app update button, and checks headless servers for updates every six hours outside playback.
Serves as the latest native desktop setup for Windows ARM64 and Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 while later V4 releases ship x64 and macOS desktop setups.

v4.2.0.title: Artwork in the room island, window-state fixes and Go security update
v4.2.0.summary: Brings profile photos and cached TMDB artwork into the watch-party island, hardens fullscreen and room transfers, and updates the Go runtime.
changes: Displays profile avatars and cached TMDB posters/backdrops inside the watch-party island with smoother motion and personal resync/offset controls.
Fixes keyboard F / Escape and title-bar double-click window restoration, revokes room file transfers immediately on leave or unfriend, and caps multi-member loading waits.
Repairs missing bundle files when re-running setup and stops deleted titles (HTTP 404 or 410) from blocking queued playback progress saves.
Rebuilds server and setup binaries with Go 1.26.9 to address standard-library security advisory GO-2026-6617.

v4.1.0.title: Synchronized watch parties across households
v4.1.0.summary: Introduces encrypted rooms for up to eight people with gentle drift correction, optional direct file streaming over WireGuard and the dynamic island.
changes: Synchronizes watch parties for up to eight participants using gentle speed nudging, a 10-second loading buffer wait, host-only or shared controls, and a per-guest cut offset.
Streams the host's file directly over encrypted WireGuard when an invited guest does not have a local copy in their own library.
Adds the dynamic island pill below the title bar, multi-interface UPnP/NAT-PMP port mapping, IPv6 friend-code endpoints and room protocol version checks.
Stops a local server started by the theia launcher automatically ten seconds after the desktop player exits.

v4.0.0.title: Profiles, friends, full-screen setup and a new foundation
v4.0.0.summary: Opens Generation 4 with household profiles, peer-to-peer WireGuard friend presence, opt-in Discord Rich Presence, a rebuilt terminal installer and PolyForm Noncommercial licensing.
changes: Adds the startup Who's watching? profile chooser, friend codes, peer-to-peer WireGuard friend presence (90-second in-memory TTL) and friends-only remote access.
Introduces opt-in local Discord Rich Presence with a separate consent toggle before sharing the title being watched.
Rebuilds theia-setup as a full-screen interactive terminal form with folder suggestions, video file counts and in-place updates keeping library and progress.
Improves filename parsing (titles, years, French release tags, multi-episode files), bundles pinned LGPL libmpv on Linux (PulseAudio/ALSA), groups settings and introduces the T-over-the-sun icon.

Moves releases from 4.0 onward to PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 with private source development (3.4.0 and earlier remain GPL-3.0 at their public tags), launches the static website, and updates source-map-js.

v3.4.0.title: Six desktop builds, rich detail pages and wrapping up V3
v3.4.0.summary: Final V3 release expanding complete desktop setups to all six OS/processor targets and adding rich film and series detail views.
changes: Publishes complete setups for all six desktop targets: Windows x64, Windows ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, Ubuntu 24.04 x64 and Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64.
Adds film and series detail pages with cached TMDB synopses, cast rails, file resolution/HDR inspection and a Windows display and GPU driver check.
Completes series episode tracking with resume bars, mark-watched/reset controls, jump to next unwatched episode and a 10-second next-episode prompt.
Allows cancelling an in-flight server connection, retries unsent playback progress saves automatically, and marks browser viewer playback feature-complete.

v3.3.6.title: Release packaging parity and macOS bundle integrity
v3.3.6.summary: Hardens release packaging with a 67-check byte-for-byte parity gate and preserves macOS framework symlinks and code signatures across extraction and updates.
changes: Enforces an exact player version match in the Windows offline ZIP and adds a 67-comparison byte-for-byte CI parity gate between standalone assets and offline bundles.
Teaches the Go ZIP extractor to recreate macOS .framework symbolic links safely and preserve 0644/0755 permissions so strict codesign verification passes.
Updates the macOS updater to swap the complete Theia.app bundle cleanly during upgrades.

v3.3.5.title: Subtitle studio, event-driven playback status and viewing statistics
v3.3.5.summary: Adds a live 1080p-scaled subtitle customizer, cuts idle playback CPU by two thirds, smooths window edge resizing and introduces viewing statistics.
changes: Adds dedicated Playback and Subtitles settings with a live 1080p-scaled preview for size, vertical position (sub-pos), colour, outline, 70% background band, font family and weight across SRT and ASS.
Replaces status polling with event-driven updates (cutting idle CPU from 2.8% to 0.9%) and defers SetWindowRgn during edge drag so window resize rises from 5 to 95 frames.
Introduces the viewing statistics dashboard with total hours watched, started/completed counts, films-to-series split bar and top series.
Adds a two-tab Languages / Quality transport popover and a collapsible volume slider.

v3.3.4.title: The native desktop player reaches Apple Silicon
v3.3.4.summary: Delivers the native macOS Apple Silicon application, installer and background launchd service, alongside deterministic reproducible builds.
changes: Ships native Theia.app on macOS Apple Silicon rendering through a libmpv OpenGL surface, installed by theia-setup-darwin-arm64 with a ~/.local/bin link and launchd service.
Preserves framework symbolic links inside the macOS offline ZIP (saving 25 MB per download) and adapts the web player transport bar cleanly below 44rem.
Removes embedded build timestamps for deterministic Go and setup binaries.

v3.3.3.title: Unified hero backdrops and rail-and-panel settings
v3.3.3.summary: Brings consistent masked backdrop artwork to Home, Films and Series, widens settings into a sectioned sheet and verifies embedded assets in CI.
changes: Unifies softened, edge-masked hero backdrop artwork across the Home, Films and Series views.
Replaces the narrow settings modal with a wider rail-and-panel sheet (Interface, Playback, Server, Update), Cancel/Save actions and a one-click copyable server URL.
Adds a CI release check confirming offline bundles embed both the compiled web interface and the TMDB key.

v3.3.2.title: The theia launcher command and clean uninstallation
v3.3.2.summary: Introduces the single theia command to start server and player together, fixes fresh empty libraries and adds clean uninstallation.
changes: Adds the theia launcher on PATH and in Windows App Paths / Start Menu, starting theia-server automatically when needed before opening theia-player.
Fixes the home view on a brand-new empty library (returning an empty rows array instead of null) so fresh installs render immediately.
Adds theia-setup --uninstall to stop running processes and remove binaries, shortcuts, registry entries and PATH changes while leaving %APPDATA%\Theia intact.

v3.3.1.title: Streamlined release downloads and build diagnostics
v3.3.1.summary: Simplifies GitHub release assets from 20 files to 9 clearly named downloads, embeds version diagnostics and patches a dependency advisory.
changes: Consolidates public release assets from 20 files down to 9 clearly labelled downloads (installer, offline bundle and updater packages) and retires the temporary 3.2 filename bridge.
Compiles and verifies the release version tag in theia-player --diagnostics and fixes a browser playback guard race condition.
Updates devalue to resolve security advisory GHSA-9rgm-9g3h-6x36.

v3.3.0.title: The native generation: server, libmpv desktop player and setup
v3.3.0.summary: Splits Theia into a local server, a native desktop player built on Tauri and pinned LGPL libmpv, and a user-space installer without administrator rights.
changes: Separates Theia into theia-server (library indexing, cached TMDB metadata and local HTTP streaming), theia-player (native Rust/Tauri desktop app) and theia-setup.

Integrates a SHA-256-pinned LGPL libmpv engine with d3d11va / gpu-next hardware decoding, Matroska, Dolby Vision Profile 7 tone-mapping, TrueHD/Atmos/DTS-HD bitstream passthrough with PCM fallback, and external plus image subtitles.
Installs in user space without administrator privileges through a six-question terminal wizard or CLI flags, verifying SHA-256 digests and supporting offline ZIP archives.
Loads the complete library payload in two local HTTP requests (measured at 0.7 seconds for 250 films).

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: No account and no telemetry. This page says exactly what leaves your computer, to whom and why, and what never does.
privacy.stays: Your library catalogue, your viewing history and your files. Theia does not upload them.
privacy.tmdb: Looks up posters, synopses and cast for the titles in your library. Results are kept on your computer.
privacy.github: Checks for updates and downloads them from the project's releases.
privacy.firebase: Runs the friends service: friend codes, profile photos, presence and opinions, through an anonymous sign-in. It connects while your server runs.
privacy.remote: Remote viewing connects your own devices directly, over WireGuard. No relay and no control plane sit in between.
privacy.drive: Theia 5 can read video files from Google Drive folders you choose. You sign in on Google's own page, so Theia never sees your Google password. The authorisation stays on the computer that runs your Theia server, and Theia only lists and streams the files you allowed, to your own devices. Nothing is sent to the maintainer. You can disconnect Drive in Theia, or revoke access in your Google account, at any time.
privacy.site: No cookies, no analytics and no remote resources. Your language choice stays in this browser. The host, like any web host, sees visitors' IP addresses in its own server logs.

about.title: About Theia
about.lead: One maintainer, a free personal media server, and plain words about how it is made.
about.icons: The interface icons and brand marks on this site are stored with it, each with its licence text.

faq.title: Good questions.
faq.intro: Straight answers before you press play. Need a hand? Find us on GitHub or Discord.

items.question: Does Theia come with films or series?
items.answer: No. Theia organises and plays video files you already have and are entitled to use. It is not a streaming catalogue and does not supply films. Posters, synopses and cast come from TMDB and are cached locally.

items.question: Is it free? Is the source public?
items.answer:
The server, library, ordinary viewing and every V4 feature are free for personal, non-commercial use. Nothing paid exists. Any future paid features, if introduced, will be announced beforehand.

Releases from 4.0 use PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; source code is developed privately and is not published. Version 3.4.0 and earlier remain GPL-3.0 with their source at the public tags. Commercial use requires a separate licence.

items.question: Which systems are supported, and what is actually tested?
items.answer:
Desktop setups exist for Windows, macOS and Ubuntu 24.04. Windows x64 is the only platform used with the maintainer's real library. The bundled 4.4.2 players passed generated-film checks on Windows, Linux x64 and hosted Macs, with Intel under Rosetta; this does not establish your screen or audio chain. Older ARM64 downloads are labelled explicitly.

Linux uses software decoding, SDR and PCM. macOS uses PCM; physical-display HDR and hardware decoding are unverified. Windows requests bitstream and falls back to PCM, but delivery of Atmos or DTS-HD MA to a receiver remains unverified. The browser viewer remains available on phones and TVs without active playback development.

items.question: Which processor should I choose?
items.answer: On Windows, open Settings → System → About and read System type: Intel/AMD means x64; an ARM processor means ARM64. On macOS, About This Mac lists either an Apple chip or an Intel processor. On Ubuntu, uname -m returns x86_64 for x64 or aarch64 for ARM64. The site selects the system only; you choose the processor.

items.question: How do I install or update Theia?
items.answer:
Download the setup for your system and processor. Choose the language, whether this computer serves, plays or does both, and your media folders. Start Theia from your launcher or with theia. On macOS and Ubuntu, make the setup executable first. Ubuntu also needs the listed desktop prerequisites.

For an update, run the new setup: your library and progress are kept. The setup and application currently support English and French, independently of this site's language.

items.question: What stays private? What leaves my computer?
items.answer:
No cloud account and no telemetry. Theia uses three external services: TMDB for film and series metadata and artwork; GitHub Releases for updates; and Firebase Realtime Database (project theia-friends, with anonymous sign-in and token renewal) solely for the friends service: friend codes, profile photos, requests, presence and opinions.

Firebase connects when the server starts and follows its inbox. It publishes directory entries for all local profiles, even before you add a friend: friend-code identifiers, names, the server public key, local profile numbers and port; photos are uploaded separately. Linked friends exchange presence, which can include the current title, episode details and artwork paths, room invitations, server version and direct tunnel addresses. You can hide the title and last-seen time. Invisible hides activity, titles, room offers and last-seen time; it does not disconnect Firebase or remove directory entries and photos. Opinions remain in recipients' inboxes until deleted or the friendship ends. Your library catalogue and viewing history are not uploaded.

Anyone who can reach port 8383 on your network can browse and administer Theia. Use a trusted network and never forward that port to the internet. This website has no analytics, remote embeds or cookies; an explicit language choice is stored only in this browser.

items.question: How do friends, rooms and remote access work?
items.answer:
Exchange friend codes, then invite friends into a private room. Remote access uses device keys and direct WireGuard connections, without a media relay or control plane. Discovery, presence and opinions use Firebase. Connectivity depends on your networks.

The maintainer reported a working two-household test session, but private rooms and the shared countdown still lack a complete real two-household validation. There is no live TV, DVR, music library, plugin system or multi-user permissions.

items.question: Where can I get help or report a problem?
items.answer: Join the project's Discord or open a GitHub issue. Include your version, system, processor and what happened. For a playback problem, add the file's video/audio formats. Share what worked, too. Never post credentials or a private library publicly; report security issues through the repository's security policy.

Open the setup from the Downloads folder.
The setup is a full-screen terminal form. First, choose English or French.
Choose this computer's role: server, player or both. Then choose your media folders.
The folder is copied from Explorer. Personal files are blurred in this recording.
Paste it into the form. The setup counts the videos in that folder.
Review the plan before anything is written. Then install.
Start Theia from the Start Menu, the Desktop or with theia in a terminal.
Windows asks whether the server may use the network. The recording allows it.
Choose who is watching. Profiles have no password.
The home screen shows the featured film and recent additions.
General settings include the application language and the startup profile chooser.
